title: Enterprise onboarding: support, escalation, integration, and QBR playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended processes and templates for enterprise onboarding, technical integration, support handoff, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support (Tier 1/2), and the Eng oncall roster.

Scope: Covers the initial 90-day onboarding timeline for Dedicated and Private customers, integration checklist for common deployment modes, standard support process, an escalation matrix with SLAs, curated known issues with workarounds, and a repeatable QBR template for health checks and executive updates.

Owners & escalation paths

- Document owner: Customer Success (Asha Patel)
- Primary contributors: Solutions Engineering, Support, Eng SRE, Product
- Contact aliases:
  - cs-redwood-enterprise@redwood.ai (primary CS queue)
  - se-predeploy@redwood.ai (pre-deployment engineering)
  - support@redwood.ai (customer support)
  - oncall-eng@redwood.ai (engineering oncall pager)

Key onboarding milestones (90-day timeline)

1) Pre-sign (Day -14 to 0)
   - Legal & Procurement checklist completed
   - High-level technical requirements captured (compute region, VPC, compliance needs, KMS)
   - Assign CS lead and SE engineer

2) Kickoff (Day 0)
   - 60-minute kickoff with agendas: goals, success metrics, SLO expectations, timeline, communication plan
   - Deliverables: project plan, integration runbook stub, access matrix

3) Integration & Testing (Day 1-30)
   - Provisioning & networking validation (VPC peering, firewall rules, egress controls)
   - Authentication & secrets (KMS/HSM integration, API key rotation policy)
   - Run functional smoke tests: token generation, streaming, embeddings, KV caching behavior
   - Security review and compliance checklist signoff

4) Performance tuning & ramp (Day 30-60)
   - Baseline perf tests (latency p50/p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens)
   - Apply Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quant profiles)
   - Load test to target throughput with rollback plan

5) Production cutover & QBR prep (Day 60-90)
   - Cutover plan, canary rollout, monitoring dashboards enabled
   - 30/60/90 day QBR materials prepared
   - Handoff to account management and long-term support plan

Integration checklist (technical)

Networking & access
- Confirm allowed IP ranges and egress rules (example: 10.0.0.0/16 allowed to 52.16.0.0/12)
- Validate VPC peering and route tables
- Verify private deployment connectivity test (TLS handshake, 3-way sync)

Authentication & secrets
- Validate KMS key policies and rotation schedule
- Confirm service principal / IAM roles with least privilege
- Document API key creation and expiration policy

Observability & monitoring
- Enable per-route latency and token-level cost dashboards in Redwood Console
- Configure alerts:
  - latency.p95 > 800ms for >5m -> paging to oncall-eng
  - errors.rate > 1% for 10m -> support escalation (Tier 1)
  - token-cost.delta > 20% week-over-week -> CS review

Testing & validation
- Smoke tests (examples): text generation end-to-end, embeddings vector similarity, streaming cancellation
- Regression tests: run customer-provided prompt-suite against model baseline and new variant
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 1 hour, validate latency, error budget

Support process (Tier definitions & SLAs)

- Tier 1 (Support): initial triage, customer communication, known-issue lookup, standard runbook execution. SLA: 1 business-hour response for P1, 4 hours for P2.
- Tier 2 (SE/CS/Dev Support): deeper debugging, log collection, reproduce and escalate. SLA: 2 business-hour response for P1 after Tier 1 triage.
- Tier 3 (Eng SRE/Product): fixes, kernel/runtime changes, hotfix releases. SLA: Eng acknowledgement within 4 business-hours of Tier 2 escalations for P1.

Priority definitions
1. P0 / Sev-1: Production outage - customer-facing application unavailable or >90% of requests failing.
2. P1 / Sev-2: Severe degradation - high error rate, major performance regression, or data loss risk.
3. P2 / Sev-3: Functional impact to important flows or intermittent failures.
4. P3 / Sev-4: Low-impact issues, feature requests, and documentation gaps.

Escalation matrix (contact & timing)

- Customer reports incident -> Support triages (0-1 hour)
- If unresolved after Tier 1 triage (30-60 minutes) or severity P0/P1 -> escalate to SE (notify via Slack #se-oncall and email se-predeploy@redwood.ai)
- If unresolved after SE analysis (60 minutes) or evidence of runtime/kernel bug -> page oncall-eng@redwood.ai and create incident in PagerDuty with severity tag
- For SLA misses or executive-impacting incidents -> notify CS leadership and CSM; prepare customer-facing incident summary within 2 business hours

Required artifacts on every escalation
- Customer ID & contact
- Exact timestamps (UTC) of first error and current time
- Request IDs, sample payloads, logs, p95/p99 latency slices
- Impact assessment and mitigation steps

Known issues & workarounds (curated)

1) Symptom: Streaming responses hang after ~30s on Private deployments
   Root cause: TLS keepalive and proxy timeouts in customer edge router
   Workaround: Update router idle timeout to 120s and enable TCP keepalives. See CLI snippet:
   curl -v --http2 https://private.redwood.example/api/v1/stream ...

2) Symptom: KV cache size grows unexpectedly causing OOMs under heavy multi-tenant usage
   Root cause: Inefficient cache eviction policy for long-tail session keys
   Workaround: Apply configuration: runtime.kv_cache.max_entries=200000 and enable runtime.kv_cache.eviction_policy=lfu. Restart runtime during low traffic window.

3) Symptom: Embedding cosine similarity drift after quantized model upgrade
   Root cause: Quantization-induced distribution shift on specific corpora
   Workaround: Use the validated quant profile labeled q8_compat and run regression test suite. Fallback to fp16 variant while evaluating.

4) Symptom: Increased 5xx errors after autoscaling policy change
   Root cause: Rapid scale-down causing stale model shards on some nodes
   Workaround: Add a 60s cool-down to autoscaler and apply pre-warm policy for model shards (prewarm=true).

Runbooks & standard playbooks

- Incident acknowledgement playbook (short):
  1) Confirm customer impact and severity.
  2) Capture snapshot of logs and metrics (console export).
  3) Execute known-issue checks.
  4) If unresolved, escalate to SE and attach artifacts.

- Production rollback playbook (when rollout regression detected):
  1) Halt rollout and stop new canary traffic.
  2) Re-route traffic to previous model version (pinned route).
  3) Reproduce regression on staging.
  4) Post-mortem owner assigned within 48 hours.

QBR & health check templates

Minimum QBR agenda (30-45m):
- Executive summary (CS): adoption, high-level health, business impact
- Usage metrics (CS/Finance): token consumption, cost per 1k tokens, top routes
- Reliability & performance (SRE): SLOs (p99 latency goal, error budget burn rate)
- Integration & roadmap (SE/Product): planned model updates, quantization roadmap
- Risks & action items (CS/Customer): blockers, compliance deadlines

Suggested QBR slides / metrics to include:
- Active users & API calls last 90 days
- Token consumption trend and cost delta vs baseline
- P50/P95/P99 latencies by route and model
- Error rates and categories (5xx, 4xx client errors)
- Open support tickets by priority and MTTR
- Action items and owners

Health check checklist (30-day recurring)
- Confirm <10% error budget burn in last 30 days
- Validate tail latency (p99) within SLO targets
- Review top-10 prompt suites for regression
- Security & compliance: review audit logs and key rotations

Communication templates

- Incident acknowledgement (email/snippet):
  Subject: Redwood Incident Acknowledgement - [Customer] - [Incident ID]
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>,

  We are investigating an issue impacting <feature>. Our initial assessment indicates <impact>. We have assigned a dedicated engineer and will provide updates every 30 minutes until resolution.

- Post-incident summary (email template)
  Body: Summary of root cause, mitigation steps taken, timeline of events (UTC), permanent remediation plan, and owner for follow-up.

Operational knobs (recommendations)

- Batching: start with target batch size 8 for NLU-style workloads and increase while validating latency SLOs
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for conversational workloads; set max_entries per-session to 10k
- Quantization: validate q8_compat on customer test-suite before enabling across fleet
- Autoscaling: aggressive scale-up, conservative scale-down (cool-down 60s)

Appendix: Example validation commands

- Connectivity check (curl):
  curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health

- Token cost export (CLI):
  redwood-cli usage export --customer <CID> --from 2026-12-01 --to 2026-12-31 --format csv

- Embedding regression test (python snippet):
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(api_key="<KEY>")
  baseline = c.embeddings.create(model="embed-1", input=["doc A"])
  new = c.embeddings.create(model="embed-1-q8_compat", input=["doc A"])
  # compute cosine and assert threshold
